chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: O sons of Abd al-Muttalib! You will never be equal to the people in their wealth, therefore meet them with the relaxed face and goodly cheerfulness.' And it is reported from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), except that he said: 'O Clan of Hashim.'

key_terms.بَنِي عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ: Sons of Abd al-Muttalib (the Prophet's clan)
key_terms.بَنِي هَاشِمٍ: Clan of Hashim (the Prophet's specific tribe)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of having a pleasant face and good cheerfulness in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic strategy of using spiritual and social grace (husn al-bashr) as a distinctive mark of the Ahl al-Bayt, compensating for their lack of material accumulation compared to the Quraysh. It underscores the Shia emphasis on character as a primary means of da'wah and social cohesion, linking the Prophet's advice to the broader ethical framework of the Imams. The variation in addressing 'Banu Abd al-Muttalib' versus 'Banu Hashim' reflects the specific lineage focus while maintaining the universal applicability of this noble trait.
